subject: [PATCH] memcg: trim the per-cpu charge stock instead of draining it

2026-08-19.patch_summary: This patch modifies the per-cpu charge stock in Linux's memory cgroup (memcg) to trim excess pages instead of draining them completely. This change addresses a performance issue where certain applications would spend an excessive amount of time charging and uncharging pages due to a corner case in the memcg code. The patch introduces two new watermarks, MEMCG_STOCK_LOW and MEMCG_STOCK_HIGH, which are used to determine when to trim excess pages from the per-cpu charge stock. This approach is similar to how the page allocator manages its own percpu caches. As a result of this change, peak cached pages per memcg will increase from 64 to 96.
